skill.name: animation-shader
skill.description: Use this skill to design, implement, and tune animation-style shaders for Unity and real-time characters. It maps visual goals to toon shader features, presets, and bundled references for lilToon, Poiyomi, UTS2, RToon, SToon, and related shader collections.
skill.summary: Plan and configure toon, cel, outline, rim, emission, dissolve, and stylized shader effects.
skill.author: Yuki001

security_audit.summary: Static analysis reported high-risk patterns, but review found Markdown shader documentation, HLSL pseudo-code, feature names, and bundled reference paths. content.value_statement: Stylized shader work can require many scattered feature decisions. This skill maps visual goals to concrete toon shader settings and references.
actual_capabilities: Maps art styles to shader features such as outlines, MatCap, rim light, dissolve, and emission.
Provides preset looks for anime, sketch, cyber, semi-realistic toon, retro, and pop art styles.
Points agents to bundled reference files for lilToon, Poiyomi, UTS2, RToon, SToon, and ToonShadingCollection.
Explains shader feature concepts with HLSL-style pseudo-code and implementation notes.
Supports planning for Unity character materials, VRChat avatars, cinematic models, and stylized effects.
limitations: It is a knowledge reference, not an automated shader compiler or material editor.
It does not test performance, rendering output, or platform compatibility inside Unity.
It may require a separate workflow skill or planning process for full project execution.
Examples describe shader concepts and may need adaptation for a specific render pipeline.

use_cases.title: Design a Toon Character Material
use_cases.description: Choose base shading, outline, rim light, MatCap, and color controls for a stylized character.

use_cases.title: Plan Avatar Shader Features
use_cases.description: Map a VRChat avatar style brief to supported lilToon or Poiyomi features and reference files.

use_cases.title: Compare Stylized Rendering Options
use_cases.description: Review which shader families support effects such as hatching, UV animation, dissolve, and AudioLink.

prompt_templates.title: Pick a Starter Style
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the animation-shader skill to recommend a starter toon shader style for a Unity character. Include the main features to enable.

prompt_templates.title: Map Features to References
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the animation-shader skill to map my desired effects to bundled reference files. Effects: outline, rim light, emission, dissolve, and MatCap.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Material Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the animation-shader skill to create a material configuration plan for a cyber anime avatar using lilToon or Poiyomi.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Stylized Shader Stack
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the animation-shader skill to review this toon shader feature stack for visual quality, performance risk, and missing references.

output_examples.input: I need a clean anime look for a mobile NPC.
output_examples.output: Recommended direction: Basic Anime. Use main texture, three-tone shading, and inverted hull outline. Avoid heavy effects such as tessellation, refraction, and complex MatCap layers.

output_examples.input: I want a cyber avatar that reacts to music.
output_examples.output: Recommended direction: Cyber VFX. Combine dark base color, emission, AudioLink modulation, dissolve, vertex glitch, and rim light. Review lilToon and Poiyomi special effect references.

output_examples.input: I need a sketch style for a flashback scene.
output_examples.output: Recommended direction: Stylized Sketch. Prioritize desaturated color adjustment, sketchy outline, hatching, halftone overlays, and paper texture layers.

best_practices: Start from a preset style, then add only the features needed for the target shot or platform.
Read every listed reference file for a selected feature before finalizing the implementation plan.
Validate complex effects in Unity with target lighting, camera distance, and performance constraints.
anti_patterns: Do not enable every advanced shader feature for a simple character material.
Do not mix shader-family settings without checking whether the target shader supports each feature.
Do not treat pseudo-code examples as drop-in production shader code.

faq.question: Does this skill generate complete shader code?
faq.answer: No. It provides shader design guidance, feature mapping, and reference material for implementation.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Which shader families are covered?
faq.answer: It covers lilToon, Poiyomi, UnityChan Toon Shader 2, RToon, SToon, and ToonShadingCollection references.

faq.question: Can it help with VRChat avatars?
faq.answer: Yes. Several presets and references are useful for avatar materials, effects, and toon rendering choices.

faq.question: Does it replace Unity testing?
faq.answer: No. You still need to test visual quality, performance, and pipeline compatibility in Unity.

faq.question: Why does it include pseudo-code?
faq.answer: The pseudo-code explains shader behavior so an agent can plan settings and implementation details.
